title: Tuples
summary: Fixed-size groups of possibly different types; destructure with (a, b) or index with .0.
lecture: A tuple groups a fixed number of values that may have different types: `(3, 7)` is a `(i32, i32)`. Two ways to get the pieces out: destructure with a pattern, `let (x, y) = point;`, or index with `.0` and `.1`.

Destructuring reads best when you use both parts; indexing is fine for a quick single access. Square-bracket patterns like `[x, y]` belong to arrays and slices, not tuples - mixing them up is error E0529.
Functions can return tuples to hand back multiple values without a struct.
